title: Hopkinton Community Center expands programs for residents | Daily-news-alerts | thewesterlysun.com
text:
HOPKINTON — Since the town’s Multipurpose Community Center officially opened in January, the Recreation Department has been expanding its programming, offering everything from after-school activities and college preparation to senior health and wellness programs, among other services.
Recreation Department Director Mary Sawyer said residents have responded positively to the new programs, while the department continues working to develop additional classes, workshops and services.
“We’ve been so busy, but all these programs are important and that’s what we are trying to do here; we’re trying to find classes, programs, and workshops that really address the needs of the community from seniors down to children,” she said. “It’s a big job, but we’ve got a great team on it, and we have some great partnerships with some local community and state organizations.”
The programming reflects the three main goals behind the creation of the community center; investing in education outside the traditional school setting, establishing public spaces for workforce development and promoting public health. The initiative received funding from several sources, including the Pandemic Recovery Office, Learn365RI and the Governor’s Community Learning Center Municipal Grant Program.
Education has been one of the center’s main areas of focus, with programs serving students ranging from elementary school children to high school seniors.
Over the summer, the community center held free financial aid and college planning courses for rising high school seniors and their families. The courses were designed to help families navigate the financial aid and college application process.
The center also offers FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid) workshops, where students and their families can sign up in advance, access printed resources and ask questions about the financial aid process. The next FAFSA event is scheduled for Oct. 6 from 6 to 7:30 p.m.
In addition to FAFSA assistance, the community center hosts a college essay writing boot camp, where students can receive help brainstorming and developing their essays. The center also offers a hands-on workshop focused on using artificial intelligence (AI) tools for research and college application projects.
College preparation is one of several educational resources available at the center. Sawyer said the Recreation Department also offers PSAT and SAT preparation classes.
For younger students, the center offers an After School Camp program Monday through Friday. Buses bring children to the community center after school, where they receive healthy snacks and can get help with their homework until their parents pick them up.
The department is also working with the Rhode Island Computer Museum to implement a video game design workshop using Scratch, a block-based programming platform that allows users to create games and other interactive projects.
The center’s programming also extends to older residents, with several health and wellness programs either already available or in development.
Sawyer said Medicare workshops are planned for the end of October. The department is also working with the Rhode Island Geriatric Education Center at the University of Rhode Island to establish its “Matter of Balance” program, which helps older adults focus on healthy lifestyle choices such as diet and fitness.
A diabetes and heart health educational series is also expected to be introduced, featuring a certified diabetes instructor.
The Recreation Department is additionally working with the Rhode Island Office of Healthy Aging and Wood River Health to implement programs focused on senior health and wellness.
Other senior activities at the center include beginner and intermediate Tai Chi lessons, chair yoga, free public access to private telehealth spaces and health checks with a registered nurse (RN) once a month.
“We have a great community of older adults and seniors that have been coming to these programs and the health and wellness programs have been especially successful,” Sawyer said. “Same thing with the computer classes for the kids, we’ve had a great turnout for FAFSA. There’s still a lot of work to do, but we are learning a lot as we go along and we’re doing our best to bring these programs and services to Hopkinton.”
Beyond its programs for children, high school students and seniors, the center also provides resources for the broader community. Residents can use private spaces for Zoom calls or job interviews, as well as computers, Wi-Fi and printers.
The Recreation Department is also working on programs involving job training, resume building and mock interviews to help residents prepare for employment opportunities.
With programs spanning education, health, workforce development and activities for residents of different ages, the community center is continuing to expand the services available to Hopkinton residents.
